title: monitor.json
description: monitor.json is how a monitor runs, and what its fix may do, from the monitor's .kiln/monitors/<name>/monitor.json. Each key may be left out. The keys recheck, mustAccept and writesTests steer a fix. A monitor with no command and no agent.md names none of them.

$schema.description: $schema names the JSON Schema an editor checks this file against: "../../monitor.schema.json", which kiln init writes to .kiln/. kiln reads nothing from it.

hours.description: hours is how often kiln monitor run runs the monitor, in whole hours from 0 to 65535, such as 1. 0 runs it at every kiln monitor run. Absent, it is 24.

recheck.description: recheck, when false, leaves the monitor's check or gauge out of its fix's gate. Use it for a problem no fix clears until it is deployed. Absent or true, the gate runs it again, and fails while it still finds the problem. A monitor with no command and no agent.md may not name it.

mustAccept.description: mustAccept, when true, keeps each fix that passes on its branch, until the developer runs kiln accept on it. Without it, a fix that passes lands on main. A monitor with no command and no agent.md may not name it.

writesTests.description: writesTests, when true, lets a fix write under each acceptance path's part before {spec}, such as uat/. Without it, a fix may not change the acceptance tests. A monitor with no command and no agent.md may not name it.

atLeast.description: atLeast is the line of the monitor's gauge, such as 80: a reading below it crossed the line. Name it or atMost beside a gauge, never both, and neither without a gauge.

atMost.description: atMost is the line of the monitor's gauge, such as 0: a reading above it crossed the line. Name it or atLeast beside a gauge, never both, and neither without a gauge.
